reviews.text: 游戏正常游玩体验没什么大问题，我只在玩最后一个武器的时候遇到过龙变人把模型卡掉的bug，其他方面的游戏内容都还差强人意。 但是本游戏并不足以让人给出好评，首先UI风格和此类游戏中最知名的throllfall完全一样，已经远不止是致敬了，以至于保留了游戏内没有图鉴和数值只有简单描述的坏习惯。其次创新点不足，游戏主要的创新点在于给武器系统增加了一些局外，让玩家本体在后期更加有用。但技能点又卡得很死，我到终局了也点不完前四级，建议多给点技能点。最后本作的BOSS战其实挺多，但存在换皮严重的问题，唯一能留下印象的只有会改变地形的BOSS有点新意，但建议给玩家点提示，否则容易初见杀。
倒是提醒我《thronefall》更新的关卡还没玩呢，内容就是thronefall的升级版，但是角色升级搞个动画还不能跳过什么意思，按空格倒是能跳过，因为直接给你把第一个选了（行吧设置里可以关，希望后续比原版更出彩吧）

首先真的，给我感觉就是完全王权陨落翻版，甚至就连美术也不如人家好看。 唯一新内容就是多了个经验条，升级了可以经典肉鸽三选一。但说真的这个也一般，第一点这个重roll就要10金币了，玩过王权陨落知道10金币真的不便宜了；然后也是技能间的平衡差，选弱的真玩不了。算是意料之内的平衡差。还有初始职业剑盾和弓也不是一个量级的，弓太幽默了，就是单纯平衡差。最后就是制作组甚至甚至不愿意加个图鉴什么的，就纯照搬，很中国人了。部分ui更王权陨落一样，甚至胜利的小bgm还是和背包乱斗一样的。最后评价是被王权陨落完爆，真的完全没有能让我花人民币的点啊

Sunbreak War is an indie strategy experience developed and published by Candlelight Studio that blends base-building, tactical combat, and roguelite progression into a tightly structured day-and-night survival loop. At its core, the game revolves around preparation and payoff. Each in-game day gives players a limited window to gather resources, expand infrastructure, and position defensive structures, while nightfall unleashes relentless enemy waves that test the resilience of those choices. This cyclical structure creates a natural tension that drives the entire experience, rewarding foresight while punishing complacency. Rather than relying purely on reflexes or overwhelming force, the game consistently asks players to think several steps ahead, making it a strategic exercise as much as a survival challenge. The gameplay loop is built around careful resource management and structural planning. During daylight phases, players construct and upgrade buildings that serve economic, defensive, or supportive roles. Every structure placement matters, as map layouts and enemy pathing influence how effectively defenses can be deployed. Some buildings focus on generating income or materials, while others strengthen frontline resistance or empower units through passive bonuses. Because there is a cap on how much can be built within each cycle, prioritization becomes critical. Deciding whether to expand production for long-term growth or invest immediately in fortifications to survive the upcoming night creates a constant strategic dilemma that remains engaging across multiple sessions. When darkness falls, Sunbreak War transitions into a more active tactical defense experience. Enemy forces advance in waves, featuring a diverse roster of monster types with varying abilities and behaviors. Some enemies swarm in numbers, others target specific structures, and certain elite foes force players to rethink their positioning on the fly. Controlling units, activating abilities, and responding to evolving threats requires attentiveness and adaptability. Combat is not purely automated; while preparation heavily influences survival odds, moment-to-moment decisions still play a significant role in determining whether a defense holds or collapses. This dynamic interplay between preparation and reaction ensures that nights feel tense and earned rather than predetermined. A defining feature of Sunbreak War is its roguelite progression system. Across runs, players unlock talents, weapons, and upgrades that meaningfully alter playstyle. Each weapon offers a distinct combat identity, supported by a talent tree that encourages experimentation. Some builds emphasize aggressive frontline dominance, while others lean into defensive synergy or economic acceleration. Because talent combinations can significantly shift how efficiently resources are used or how effectively enemies are countered, replayability becomes one of the game’s strongest assets. Failed runs rarely feel wasted, as accumulated unlocks and lessons learned inform future strategies. This steady sense of progression motivates players to refine tactics and attempt increasingly difficult maps. Visually, the game embraces a stylized aesthetic that prioritizes clarity over photorealism. The environments are cleanly designed, making building placement and enemy movement easy to track even during chaotic night sequences. Monster designs are varied enough to provide visual distinction between threat types, which is crucial for quick tactical recognition. While the art direction does not aim for cutting-edge fidelity, it succeeds in supporting gameplay readability and maintaining a cohesive atmosphere. Performance remains stable, allowing the strategic systems to remain the focal point without distraction from technical instability. Pacing is one of the game’s most compelling strengths. The alternating calm of daytime planning and the urgency of nighttime combat creates a satisfying rhythm. Each cycle builds anticipation, and the gradual escalation of enemy difficulty ensures that complacency is rarely an option. As players progress through the game’s maps, new environmental challenges and enemy combinations introduce fresh variables, preventing strategies from becoming overly formulaic. This escalating complexity encourages creative adaptation rather than reliance on a single optimal build. However, Sunbreak War is not without its potential drawbacks. The heavy emphasis on strategic planning may feel overwhelming to players who prefer more action-driven or forgiving gameplay. Early mistakes can compound quickly, and some difficulty spikes may require multiple attempts to decipher the most effective counter-strategy. Additionally, while the thematic framing provides context for the conflict, narrative depth takes a backseat to mechanics. Players seeking a rich story with deep character development may find the lore relatively understated compared to the robust gameplay systems. Overall, Sunbreak War stands as a thoughtful hybrid of strategy, base-building, and roguelite design. Its strength lies in the deliberate interplay between preparation and execution, offering a rewarding loop that encourages experimentation and long-term mastery. The combination of structured progression, tactical depth, and escalating challenge makes it particularly appealing to players who enjoy refining strategies across multiple runs. While it may not cater to those looking for narrative-heavy experiences or casual accessibility, it delivers a focused and engaging strategy experience that rewards patience, foresight, and creative problem-solving. Rating: 8/10

Gameplay is about surviving all the nights against a relentless enemy that keeps coming in greater numbers with each wave. The only unit under your control is the hero, who attacks enemies automatically when you get near and has a special skill that must go through a cooldown period after each use. Your run ends when your town center is destroyed, but you earn coins from enemies that can be used to upgrade the base and build new structures. For instance, you can build houses or granaries that earn coins after each night, towers that help deal damage to approaching enemies, or barracks that produce soldiers. Each building can also be upgraded to boost its health and coin or unit generation. However, structure placement is preset for each building on each map, so the only strategy is deciding which one to build first. In addition, a building can only be upgraded to a level that matches the town center. If you want to progress further, you will first have to spend a lot of coins upgrading the main building. As a commander, you control troop placement. You can either order them to follow or to stand their ground and defend a position. A convenient feature is that you do not have to run around the map to gather your troops. You can simply press a button to teleport them to your location. Placement is vital because you can see enemy entry points before the start of each night, and you can even see what types of enemies each entry point will spawn, allowing you to prepare accordingly. If there is only one entry point, you can focus everyone there. If there are several, you can spread your units around. The most dangerous enemies are flying units, which attack from behind and destroy your coin generating structures, and fast enemies that can slip past your slow knights. Every enemy killed, whether by the hero, unit, or tower, grants experience that eventually leads to a level up for your hero. This allows you to choose one upgrade from a random selection of three. These upgrades can affect your hero, units, or structures. For example, you can increase the hero’s attack speed, upgrade a tower into a cannon or allow it to fire two arrows, boost units when the hero is nearby, and more. You decide when to start the night, so there is no time pressure. There is also no need to worry about lost units because each fallen soldier is automatically replaced from the barracks. The spawn speed depends on the structure’s level, and units heal after each night. Although your hero can be knocked out, they respawn on the spot after a few seconds. When a stage is won, you enter a map where you can pick the next stage or replay previous ones to complete challenges. Challenges are modifiers that make stages tougher, such as increased enemy damage or speed. You can activate as many as you want to increase your overall score, but some challenges unlock only after you complete specific stages. In addition to modifiers, some challenges require you to pick a certain weapon or perk, or upgrade a specific structure to the required level. The challenges for each stage are known in advance, so you can attempt one or two on your first try or tackle them separately. Each completed challenge rewards you with a star that can be used to buy permanent upgrades for your hero. However, upgrades are tied to the six weapons, more specifically to their perks. You start with a sword and shield, then unlock a bow after the first stage, followed by four more weapons as you progress. Only one weapon can be equipped before the start of a stage, and it determines the skill you can use. Each weapon has five perks, and each perk can be upgraded five times. For example, the bow can gain a chance to deal extra damage or fire two arrows, while the starting sword and shield combo can deal splash damage or trigger an explosion after using a skill. Each upgrade costs one additional star, but your choices are not permanent because you can reset your stars and reassign them to different perks or powers.

[h1] 极具潜力的“英雄增强版”Thronefall：虽有瑕疵但值得一试 [/h1] [b]总体评价：[/b] 这是一款非常优秀的塔防策略游戏！核心玩法可以概括为“白天花钱搞基建，晚上亲自守家”。虽然在玩法框架上与《Thronefall》相似，但这并不意味着它缺乏独特性。由于英雄系统的存在，游戏体验有着显著的区别。即便是《Thronefall》的老玩家，我也依然强烈推荐本作。 [hr][/hr] [h2]✔ 优点[/h2] [list] [*] [b]出色的英雄设计：[/b] 英雄的加入让原本静态的塔防模式变得灵动且有趣。玩家不再只是一个指挥官，更是战场上的“救火队员”，夜晚在各个防区穿梭支援，极大地提升了游戏的参与感和紧张感。 [/list] [h2]✘ 缺点与改进建议[/h2] [olist] [*] [b]天赋路线缺乏多样性：[/b] 每种武器的天赋升级路径过于单一，缺乏分支选择。这导致目前的加点思路基本只有一种“最优解”，限制了玩家尝试不同流派的空间。 [*] [b]局外成长数值平衡性有待商榷：[/b] 挑战获得的“能力点”仅能强化英雄武器，对兵种和建筑毫无提升。这导致了一个极端现象：在能力点充裕的后期，部分武器强度过高（如[弓箭]可以3秒内打完boss三管血）；而在点数匮乏的前期，部分武器又显得极其乏力，体验落差较大。 [*] [b]兵种微操体验仍需优化：[/b] [list] [*] [u]紧急调度不便：[/u] 当夜晚某一侧路口失守需要救援时，目前只能亲自跑过去按R带兵，或者按全图快捷键（1-4）喊全家老小过来，缺乏局部快速调度的手段。 [*] [u]分兵操作繁琐：[/u] 白天布阵时，单一的R键操作不够细腻。比如想把4个小兵平分成两组，目前的判定非常考验操作精度，建议增加更便捷的分兵逻辑。 [/list] [*] [b]数据可视化严重缺失：[/b] 目前的数值反馈非常模糊。玩家无法查看不同兵种的具体血量、攻防差异；防御塔升级时，除了血量增加外，攻击力、投射物数量等提升均不透明。更重要的是，[i]缺乏战后结算数据[/i]——不知道每个兵种整晚贡献了多少伤害，很难判断谁是主力，谁在“混日子”。 [*] [b]大地图引导与全局视角：[/b] 游戏地图大、可造建筑多本是好事，但缺乏有效的全局视角。由于引导不足，进入新地图时很容易漏掉某些角落的经济建筑（比如玩到后期才发现漏造了两个渔船码头）。目前不得不为了查漏补缺，在每次升级主城后都要强行绕图跑一圈，体验略显疲劳。 [/olist] [hr][/hr] [h3] 总结 [/h3] 《破晓战纪》在致敬经典的同时做出了自己的特色，虽然在操作细节和数值透明度上还有路要走，但瑕不掩瑜。

So yeah, this is totally just a Thronefall clone. Thronefall definitely has more challenge, scaling, polish, and much better ui than this. If you want to play this type of game and haven't played Thronefall yet, go do that, it's amazing. That being said, this is also not a bad game. While I do think it needs tighter difficulty for risk/reward in building economic / military buildings (especially since it gives you roguelite progression as an extra handicap), I haven't run into any game breaking issues or irritants. It's made well enough, just short the tuning. If you want to scratch that nightly defense itch, go for it, it's cheap on sale (and even full price, really).
搭建防线，抵御怪物的入侵，直到黎明来临。《破晓战纪》，这是一款非常有意思的3D俯视角策略塔防游戏。相对于传统塔防，本作引入了肉鸽升级以及多样化兵种军队，这两者搭配原本塔防元素让游戏的乐趣成倍提高。此外通过移动与空格键就能完成大部分操作，比如建造/升级建筑和使用技能。这点的设计大大降低了操作负担，让我们能更专注于资源分配、兵种搭配和战场布局，值得感兴趣的玩家来尝试体验。
